note: Design vocabulary and the checks that decide whether a prompt is likely to produce a good clip. Every entry cites where it came from; nothing here is a style opinion of this project's own.

sources.veo: Veo video generation prompt guide (Google Cloud) — cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/video/video-gen-prompt-guide
sources.veo_bp: Best practices for generating videos (Google Cloud) — cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/video/best-practice

camera_move.label: Camera move — exactly one
camera_move.evidence: Camera movements: static shot, pan (left/right), tilt (up/down), dolly (in/out), truck (left/right), pedestal (up/down), zoom (in/out), crane shot, aerial shot, handheld, whip pan, arc shot.

shot_size.label: Shot size
shot_size.evidence: 镜头尺寸 defaults: '若无特殊要求，默认选择 Medium shot 或 Wide shot' — if nothing is specified, Medium or Wide is chosen for you.

lens.label: Lens / optics
lens.evidence: Lens and optical effects: wide-angle, telephoto, shallow depth of field (bokeh), deep depth of field, lens flare, rack focus, fisheye, vertigo effect (dolly zoom). 'Some advanced camera lenses are not officially supported.'

light_source.label: Light source
light_source.evidence: 光源: Daylight, Artificial lighting, Moonlight, Practical lighting, Firelight, Fluorescent lighting, Overcast lighting, Sunny lighting — '根据室内室外及prompt内容选定义光源' (inferred from the scene).

light_quality.label: Light quality and angle
light_quality.evidence: 光线强度: Soft lighting, Hard lighting. 光线角度: Top lighting, Side lighting, Underlighting, Edge lighting.

tone.label: Colour tone
tone.evidence: 色调: Warm colors, Cool colors, Mixed colors.

time_of_day.label: Time of day
time_of_day.evidence: 时间: Day time, Night time, Dawn time, Sunrise time — '如果prompt没有特别说明则选 Day time!!!' (Day time is the default if you say nothing).

composition.label: Composition
composition.evidence: 构图: Center composition, Balanced composition, Right-heavy composition, Left-heavy composition, Symmetrical composition, Short-side composition — '若无特殊要求，默认选择Center composition'.

style.label: Look / format
style.evidence: Style is one of the most powerful levers: '1970s film', 'epic, IMAX-scale scene', '16mm black-and-white film'. 'Establish this style early so the model can carry it through consistently.'

negative.label: Negative prompt — nouns only
negative.evidence: Negative prompts: 'Not recommended: using instructive language or words such as "no" or "don't"... Recommended: describe what you don't want to see. For example, "wall, frame".'

audio.label: Audio
audio.evidence: Dialogue must be described in the prompt, in a block below the prose, with short natural lines labelled by speaker. 'If your shot is silent, you can still suggest pacing with one small sound... Think of it as a rhythm cue rather than a full soundtrack.'

checks.title: Resolution, duration or aspect requested in the prompt text
checks.why: These are API parameters. The model will not change them because you asked in prose.
checks.fix: Move it to the parameter block (size / seconds / aspect_ratio) and delete it from the prompt.
checks.evidence: 'The prompt controls the content of the video, but certain attributes are governed only by API parameters. You cannot request them in prose, they must be set explicitly in your API call.'

checks.title: Words that describe a feeling instead of a picture
checks.why: The model cannot see 'beautiful'. It can see wet asphalt and neon reflections.
checks.fix: Replace each one with what the camera would actually record.
checks.evidence: Weak: 'A beautiful street at night'. Strong: 'Wet asphalt, zebra crosswalk, neon signs reflecting in puddles'. 'Clarity wins... Verbs and nouns that point to visible results will always give you a clearer, more consistent output.'

checks.title: 'Cinematic' with no technical reason
checks.why: On its own it is a feeling. Cinema comes from lens, light and grade.
checks.fix: Name the lens, the lighting and the grade — or drop the word.
checks.evidence: Weak: 'Camera shot: cinematic look'. Strong: 'wide shot, low angle / shallow DOF / warm backlight with soft rim'.

checks.title: More than one scene in a short clip
checks.why: Chaining A then B then C in one short video usually produces something muddled.
checks.fix: Keep one moment per clip; generate the second beat as its own clip and stitch.
checks.evidence: 'For short videos, dedicate each prompt to a single, focused moment. Trying to chain multiple distinct events (A then B then C) in one prompt for a short video often leads to muddled or incomplete videos.'

checks.title: Two camera moves, or opposing ones
checks.why: One shot has one camera move. Opposing moves fight each other and the frame wobbles.
checks.fix: Keep the single move that serves the shot and delete the others.
checks.evidence: 拍摄角度: '若原始prompt中有运镜的描述，则取消添加此项' — if the prompt already has a camera move, the director prompt adds none. Sora: 'Each shot should have one clear camera move and one clear subject action.'

checks.title: Action with no beats
checks.why: Motion is the hardest part to get right; vague verbs leave the model to improvise timing.
checks.fix: Describe the action in beats, with counts or timings.
checks.evidence: Weak: 'Actor walks across the room'. Strong: 'Actor takes four steps to the window, pauses, and pulls the curtain in the final second.'

checks.title: No lighting described
checks.why: Light sets the mood more than the action does, and it is what holds a multi-clip edit together.
checks.fix: Add light direction and quality, plus three to five colour anchors.
checks.evidence: Weak: 'Lighting + palette: brightly lit room'. Strong: 'soft window light with warm lamp fill, cool rim from hallway. Palette anchors: amber, cream, walnut brown.'

checks.title: Speech in quotation marks
checks.why: Quotes tend to make the model render the words as on-screen text.
checks.fix: Use a colon after the speaker's action instead: 'A woman says: My name is Clara.'
checks.evidence: 'To prevent the model from rendering text in the video, use a colon (:) after the speaker's action to denote speech and avoid using quotation marks.'

checks.title: More speech than the clip can hold
checks.why: A four-second shot fits one or two short exchanges; longer speeches break the pacing and the lip sync.
checks.fix: Cut the lines down, or lengthen the clip.
checks.evidence: 'A 4-second shot will usually accommodate one or two short exchanges, while an 8-second clip can support a few more. Long, complex speeches are unlikely to sync well.'

checks.title: Negative phrasing inside the prompt
checks.why: Negative prompts work as noun lists. 'No walls' reads as an instruction about walls.
checks.fix: Put the unwanted nouns in the negative prompt field: 'wall, frame'.
checks.evidence: Negative prompts: 'Not recommended: using instructive language or words such as "no" or "don't". For example, avoid prompts such as "no walls" or "don't show walls". Recommended: describe what you don't want to see... "wall, frame".'

checks.title: Prose about the feeling of the scene
checks.why: The models that expand prompts are explicitly told to leave this out; it costs you tokens and adds nothing the camera can record.
checks.fix: Say what happens and how it looks. Cut the atmosphere sentence.
checks.evidence: Rule 3: '不要输出关于氛围、感觉等文学描写' — do not output literary descriptions of atmosphere or feeling.

checks.title: Nothing moves
checks.why: A video model needs motion to animate. A static description of a beautiful object gives it almost nothing to do.
checks.fix: Add one action, or at least a background movement: drifting cloud, wind in leaves, steam.
checks.evidence: Rule 4: describe how the motion happens; if there is no action, add one, and background elements may carry suitable motion too.

checks.title: Prompt length is outside the range the model owners target
checks.why: Wan's expander aims at 80–100 words. Very long prompts restrict the model's own choices; very short ones leave everything open.
checks.fix: Aim for one paragraph that covers subject, action, camera, light and sound.
checks.evidence: Rule 7: 'The revised prompt should be around 80-100 words long.' Sora: 'Longer, more detailed prompts restrict the model's creativity.'

image_reference.evidence: Image input: 'Include an image file as the input_reference parameter... The image must match the target video's resolution (size). Supported file formats are image/jpeg, image/png, and image/webp.' Characters API: upload a 2-4s, 720p-1080p, 16:9 or 9:16 MP4 to reuse a character; 'We recommend no more than 2 characters per generation.'
rules: An image locks composition, wardrobe and look. Put your effort into the image, then describe only what changes in it.
Describe motion and camera only — never re-describe what is already visible in the frame.
The image must match the target resolution, and it becomes the first frame unless the model says otherwise.
Keep the subject wording identical across shots; that is what holds continuity together.

motion_only_rule.evidence: I2V prompt: 'Your rewritten video description should retain the dynamic parts of the provided prompts, focusing on the main subject's actions... Retain and emphasize descriptions of camera movements.'

labelled.label: Labelled blocks (OpenAI's documented shape)
labelled.evidence: Prompt template: '[Prose scene description...] Cinematography: Camera shot: / Mood: / Actions: - ... Dialogue: ...'

inline.label: One compact paragraph
inline.evidence: The Wan expander rewrites into a single 80-100 word paragraph rather than labelled blocks.
